facts.label: Quarterly reports, Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 (10-Q)
facts.text: - Periods: page:1 of each states "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026", "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026" and "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026" respectively. Q3 contains the statements of comprehensive income (page:2), balance sheet (page:3), cash flows (page:4) and notes (pages 6-28). Discrete quarters for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 are each available from their own report; a fourth-quarter 2025 figure is not printed in any supplied source as a discrete quarter and would have to be derived downstream. - Debt detail at facility level, Q3 (page:13): "2031 Revolver $ 79 $ 657", "Term Loan B due 2033 500 —", "2027 Senior Notes 600 600", "2028 Senior Notes 700 700", "2030 Senior Notes 1,200 1,200", "2031 Senior Notes 600 600", "Total debt 4,748 5,155". Coupons and maturities for each note series are in the same note (page:16) and again in the MD&A (pages 47-48). - Revolver availability, Q3 (page:14): "The Company had $1.1 billion available borrowing capacity, after consideration of $10 million in outstanding letters of credit, under the 2031 Revolver as of September 30, 2026." The text gives availability rounded to $0.1 billion, not to the million. - Cash paid, Q3 (page:4): "Cash paid for interest $ 173 $ 193" and "Cash paid for income taxes 65 17" for the nine months of 2026 and 2025. The Q1 report prints "Cash paid for interest $ 43 $ 45" and the Q2 report prints "Cash paid for interest $ 139 $ 145" on their own cumulative bases (three and six months). Cash-paid interest and tax are therefore available on a year-to-date basis for each 2026 report; a stand-alone Q2 or Q3 figure would have to be derived downstream. - Quarter versus year-to-date: Q3 prints three-month and nine-month columns side by side (page:2, "Total net revenue 696 683 2,339 2,260"). Q2 prints three-month and six-month columns. Downstream work must keep the two bases separate. - Segment and adjusted measures: three reportable segments, plus All Other (Q3 page:25-27), and Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation in the MD&A (page:35: "Adjusted EBITDA 264 262 2 998 958 40"). - Subsequent events in Q3 (page:28): "On October 19, 2026, the Company redeemed the 2027 Senior Notes with borrowings from the 2031 Revolver." The balance sheet date figures therefore pre-date that redemption, and the 2027 Senior Notes line of "600" is outstanding at September 30, 2026 but not at the report date. Same page: a dividend and a repurchase authorization declared October 27, 2026. - Net debt in the MD&A is a company definition: page:44 "Net debt $ 4,063 $ 5,067 $ (1,004)" is total debt net of current maturities and issuance costs, and is not net of cash. It differs from the "net bank leverage" metric in the releases. - Covenant disclosure: the Q1, Q2 and Q3 reports do not contain a covenant table or a compliance statement. A text search of those three reports for "compliant" and "interest coverage ratio" returned no hits. Only the risk-factor and forward-looking statement language about covenants appears.

facts.label: Earnings releases, Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 (Exhibit 99.1)

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable for CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 on the consolidated Churchill Downs Incorporated perimeter. Facility-level debt, the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation for FY2025 and nine months 2026, cash flow and cash-paid interest and tax are printed in filed statements. On those figures, total debt at September 30, 2026 was 4,748 million and unrestricted cash 167 million. Last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA computed here is 1,245.3 million, giving 3.81x gross and 3.68x net of unrestricted cash. That compares with 4.28x gross and 4.11x net at year-end 2025 on the same method, so leverage fell materially over nine months. The reduction is real in principal terms but involves three pieces that a reader must keep apart: repaid revolver and term loan B-1 borrowings, a new term loan B, and a subsequent-event shift of 600 million of note debt onto the revolver. The view is restricted in three respects: covenant levels are available only at December 31, 2025; the governing legal documents are not in the pack; and the last-twelve-months build mixes sources printed to one decimal (FY2025) with whole-million sources. No restriction blocks the downstream modules.

facts.label: Leverage
facts.text: On the method used here, gross leverage fell from 4.28x at December 31, 2025 to 3.81x at September 30, 2026 and net leverage from 4.11x to 3.68x. Secured debt (revolver, Term Loan A and Term Loan B) is 1,648, which is 1.32x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA gross, and about 34.7% of total debt. At December 31, 2025 the company reported a covenant secured net leverage ratio of 1.4x against a limit of 4.0x. The same secured-debt arithmetic on year-end figures gives 1.54x net of unrestricted cash, so covenant definitions (EBITDA, cash netting, letters of credit) differ from the metric computed here by an unexplained margin. Evidence to risk to implication: Adjusted EBITDA includes affiliate EBITDA that is not cash to the issuer, so leverage on a cash basis is higher than the ratios above; the subsequent-event shift of 600 of notes to the revolver does not change total debt but raises the secured share.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Churchill Downs Incorporated is a Kentucky-incorporated, Nasdaq-listed operator whose earnings come from three segments: Live and Historical Racing, Wagering Services and Solutions, and Gaming. Live and Historical Racing, which combines the Kentucky Derby franchise with historical racing machine venues in Kentucky, Virginia and New Hampshire, is the largest segment by revenue and Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026. Gaming is the second largest and carries the equity income from two unconsolidated casinos. The company is publicly owned with no controlling holder disclosed in the supplied text, so no sponsor behaviour is inferred; governance is assessed from documented issuer actions only. The most important transaction fact for a creditor is the July 29, 2026 announcement that the company is exploring a sale of nine wholly owned regional gaming properties, set against a recently refinanced bank structure, a pending note redemption funded by the revolver, an active growth capital program and a larger buyback authorization. These pull in different directions for creditors: asset-sale proceeds and lower buybacks would reduce leverage, while the growth program and buybacks would absorb cash. Confidence is Medium because the sale has no disclosed terms.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Concentration and seasonality. Evidence: nine-month 2026 historical racing revenue of 780 is 33.3% of group revenue, Churchill Downs Racetrack revenue is 262 in nine months but 12 in Q3, and the second quarter produced 477 of the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 998 (47.8%). Mechanic: earnings and the revolver draw are tied to the Derby calendar and to Virginia and Kentucky machine regulation, so a stand-alone quarter misstates run-rate and one regulatory or tax change can move group cash flow. Implication: leverage tolerance and liquidity should be judged on LTM and seasonal-peak working capital, and monitoring should track Virginia tax and competition. No logged conflict counters this. 2. Portfolio review. Evidence: the Q3 10-Q p32 statement and the Gaming segment Adjusted EBITDA of 384 for nine months, of which 143 is equity income that would not be part of a sale of wholly owned properties. Mechanic: a sale of 280 to 300 of annual Adjusted EBITDA removes 22.5% to 24.1% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 1,245.3. At the 3.68x net leverage of CP-1, proceeds of about 1,030 to 1,104 would be needed to leave net leverage unchanged if all proceeds repaid debt and nothing else changed; this is an illustrative threshold, not a valuation or a forecast. Implication: the debt-reduction benefit depends on proceeds, tax leakage and any mandatory prepayment or collateral-release terms, none supplied; the remaining company would be more concentrated in racing and historical racing machines. No logged conflict counters this. 3. Capital allocation. Evidence: FY2025 outflows exceeded free cash flow with net borrowings of 216.4, followed by 2026 deleveraging and a 750 authorization. Mechanic: buybacks are discretionary and can be paced to leverage; project capital is guided at 160 to 180 for 2026 with Rockingham at 180 to 200 and a 280 to 300 Churchill Downs Racetrack building announced (10-K p58). Implication: no sponsor-style extraction is evident, but the board has shown it will let total debt rise while returning cash and buying assets, so monitoring posture should follow leverage targets and revolver usage. No logged conflict counters this.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The refinancing completed in the quarter has four parts. On September 25, 2026 the company closed the eighth amendment to its credit agreement, extending the maturity of the revolver and Term Loan A from July 2029 to September 2031, removing the 10 basis point credit spread adjustment and amending other provisions, with the extension subject to a springing maturity if notes or other material debt maturing before September 25, 2031 are not refinanced at least 91 days before maturity (Q3 10-Q page:14). On the same date it entered a new 500 million senior secured term loan B due September 25, 2033 under the credit agreement, issued at 99.875% of principal at SOFR plus 175 basis points with quarterly amortization of 0.25% of the original balance; net proceeds were used to repay the Term Loan B-1 due 2028, to repay revolver borrowings, to pay fees and for working capital and general corporate purposes (page:14 and page:15). Debt issuance costs of 7 were paid in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:4). Third, on September 18, 2026 the company issued a conditional notice to redeem the 600 million 5.50% senior notes due April 1, 2027, and on October 19, 2026 it redeemed them with revolver borrowings, a subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet (pages 16 and 28). The redemption price and accrued interest are not supplied. Fourth, it declared an annual dividend of $0.469 per share payable January 5, 2027 and approved a new 750 million repurchase program that includes the 306 million remaining under the prior program (page:28).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Churchill Downs Incorporated is a sound, moderately leveraged credit whose direction depends on how it uses the next year's cash. The strongest support is deleveraging: net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.11x to 3.68x, free cash flow was USD 529.9 million and liquidity was USD 1,278 million at September 30, 2026. The weakest point is that the cushion can be spent: a USD 750 million buyback authorization, USD 545 to 585 million of announced projects and a possible sale of assets worth USD 280 to 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA all compete with debt reduction, while the 2027 notes now sit on the revolver. The outcome turns on sale proceeds, buyback pace and refinancing the 2028 notes before about October 2027. Confidence: Medium.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Churchill Downs reduced total debt from USD 5,155 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 4,748 million at September 30, 2026, and its net leverage on LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,245.3 million fell from 4.11x to 3.68x (gross 4.28x to 3.81x). The reduction came from operating cash flow of USD 660 million in nine months after capital expenditures of USD 176 million, and from sharply lower buybacks of USD 44 million against USD 396 million a year earlier. LTM free cash flow before distributions was USD 529.9 million, and Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest 4.54x, up from 4.09x at year-end 2025.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The most consequential new fact is the July 29, 2026 announcement that the company is exploring a sale of nine wholly owned gaming properties representing USD 280 to 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA, or 22.5% to 24.1% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA. At the current 3.68x net leverage, sale proceeds of roughly USD 1,030 to 1,104 million used to repay debt would leave leverage unchanged; any lower price would raise it, any higher price would reduce it. Terms, buyer, timetable and use of proceeds are not disclosed, and the creditor consequences of mandatory prepayment or collateral release cannot be assessed without the credit agreement.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The September 2026 refinancing extended the revolver and Term Loan A to September 2031 and added a USD 500 million term loan B due 2033 that retired the 2028 term loan, but it left a springing maturity: if notes maturing before September 25, 2031 are not refinanced 91 days ahead, the bank debt matures earlier. For the USD 700 million 2028 notes that date is about October 16, 2027. The USD 600 million 2027 notes were redeemed on October 19, 2026 with revolver borrowings, a subsequent event; illustratively that cuts revolver availability from USD 1,111 million to USD 511 million and liquidity from USD 1,278 million to USD 678 million if nothing else changed. Even so, computed secured net leverage after the redemption is about 1.67x against a December 2025 covenant limit of 4.0x, and the reported December 2025 interest coverage of 3.9x compares with a 2.5x minimum, so maintenance covenant pressure is not evident, although 2026 covenant figures are not supplied.

facts.text: Earnings quality and concentration deserve weight. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Churchill Downs operates Churchill Downs Racetrack, home of the Kentucky Derby, within a diversified portfolio across racing, historical racing, online wagering and regional casinos, with three segments each producing Adjusted EBITDA. Cash conversion is strong: LTM operating cash flow of USD 755.8 million is 60.7% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow is 42.6%. Gross leverage on the LTM basis has fallen at every quarter-end of 2026, from 4.28x in December 2025 to 4.07x in March, 3.86x in June and 3.81x in September 2026. Liquidity of USD 1,278 million and maintenance covenants with wide computed cushions give room, and the bank maturity extension to 2031, subject to the springing maturity, removes near-term bank refinancing. At September 30, 2026 about 34.7% of debt was secured and 65.3% was unsecured notes, and after the October 2026 redemption no note matures until January 2028.

Buybacks and projects are discretionary but large, and the portfolio review would remove about a quarter of earnings before any deleveraging is certain.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Secured debt after the October 19, 2026 redemption, illustrative: 1,648 + 600 = 2,248 (USD millions); secured net leverage (2,248 - 167) / 1,245.3 = 1.67x. This assumes the redemption was funded at principal entirely by the revolver and no other balance changed. 2. Interest-coverage cushion: reported December 31, 2025 coverage 3.9x against a 2.5x minimum; EBITDA could fall by (3.9 - 2.5) / 3.9 = 35.9% with interest unchanged before the covenant ratio reached the minimum. On the simple LTM ratio of 4.34x (1,245.3 / 286.7) the equivalent fall is 1 - 2.5 / 4.34 = 42.4%, to EBITDA of 716.8. Covenant definitions are not supplied, so these are indicative only. 3. Cash conversion: LTM operating cash flow 755.8 / 1,245.3 = 60.7%; LTM free cash flow 529.9 / 1,245.3 = 42.6%. 4. Leverage trend, from CP-1 chart data: gross 4.28x (December 2025), 4.07x (March 2026), 3.86x (June 2026), 3.81x (September 2026); net 4.11x, 3.90x, 3.70x, 3.68x. 5. Equity-affiliate bridge, nine months 2026: Adjusted EBITDA contribution 143 = equity income in the income statement 115 + affiliate interest, depreciation and amortization 28; distributions received 106; undistributed equity income 115 - 106 = 9; 143 - 106 = 37 = 28 + 9. Distributions as a share of equity income 106 / 115 = 92.2%. 6. FY2025 funding gap: free cash flow 494.9 less dividends 30.8, repurchases 427.8, share-settlement taxes 17.0 and acquisition of gaming rights 185.3 = -166.0; net borrowings 216.4. 7. Portfolio review weight and leverage-neutral proceeds: 280 / 1,245.3 = 22.5%; 300 / 1,245.3 = 24.1%; 3.679 x 280 = 1,030; 3.679 x 300 = 1,104 (illustrative, all proceeds repaying debt). 8. Debt change: 4,748 - 5,155 = -407. Growth amounts: 545 to 585.

### Readiness view

The effective source set supports a credit snapshot on the consolidated Churchill Downs Incorporated perimeter. The annual report and three quarterly reports are filed statements and control over the releases. The set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the requested modules: the owner of each module can perform its method, with bounded gaps on covenants, executed legal terms, guarantor and restricted-group perimeter, and management guidance. No source is blocked, and no missing downstream handoff is treated as a source condition. This view concerns source sufficiency only (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY); it does not evaluate any downstream input contract, normalize quarters or reconcile figures.
### Per-source assessment
#### Annual report, FY2025 (10-K)

- Identity and perimeter: the cover states "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025" (page:1), and the registrant is Churchill Downs Incorporated, a single consolidated reporting entity. Evidence: statements and notes are in the pack (balance sheet at page:78, debt note at pages 108-113, segment note at pages 123-127, auditor's report at pages 128-131, exhibit index at pages 135-141).

- Controlling facts: audited FY2025 statements and the only printed financial-covenant table. Page:69 states "The Credit Agreement also contains financial covenants providing for the maintenance of a maximum consolidated secured net leverage ratio and maintenance of a minimum consolidated interest coverage ratio." and tabulates "Interest coverage ratio 3.9 to 1.0 > 2.5 to 1.0" and "Consolidated total secured net leverage ratio 1.4 to 1.0 < 4.0 to 1.0"; page:70 states "The Company was compliant with all applicable covenants on December 31, 2025."

- Unit basis: this source prints one decimal (for example "Total debt 5,155.1 4,938.7 216.4"), while the quarterly reports print whole millions. Cross-period tie-outs will carry rounding differences of that size.
- Limitation: the exhibit index at page:140 lists "10.26 Credit Agreement, dated as of December 27, 2017" by reference only; the agreement is not in the pack.
#### Quarterly reports, Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 (10-Q)

- Periods: page:1 of each states "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026", "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026" and "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026" respectively. Q3 contains the statements of comprehensive income (page:2), balance sheet (page:3), cash flows (page:4) and notes (pages 6-28). Discrete quarters for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 are each available from their own report; a fourth-quarter 2025 figure is not printed in any supplied source as a discrete quarter and would have to be derived downstream.

- Debt detail at facility level, Q3 (page:13): "2031 Revolver $ 79 $ 657", "Term Loan B due 2033 500 —", "2027 Senior Notes 600 600", "2028 Senior Notes 700 700", "2030 Senior Notes 1,200 1,200", "2031 Senior Notes 600 600", "Total debt 4,748 5,155". Coupons and maturities for each note series are in the same note (page:16) and again in the MD&A (pages 47-48).

- Revolver availability, Q3 (page:14): "The Company had $1.1 billion available borrowing capacity, after consideration of $10 million in outstanding letters of credit, under the 2031 Revolver as of September 30, 2026." The text gives availability rounded to $0.1 billion, not to the million.

- Cash paid, Q3 (page:4): "Cash paid for interest $ 173 $ 193" and "Cash paid for income taxes 65 17" for the nine months of 2026 and 2025. The Q1 report prints "Cash paid for interest $ 43 $ 45" and the Q2 report prints "Cash paid for interest $ 139 $ 145" on their own cumulative bases (three and six months). Cash-paid interest and tax are therefore available on a year-to-date basis for each 2026 report; a stand-alone Q2 or Q3 figure would have to be derived downstream.

- Quarter versus year-to-date: Q3 prints three-month and nine-month columns side by side (page:2, "Total net revenue 696 683 2,339 2,260"). Q2 prints three-month and six-month columns. Downstream work must keep the two bases separate.
- Segment and adjusted measures: three reportable segments, plus All Other (Q3 page:25-27), and Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation in the MD&A (page:35: "Adjusted EBITDA 264 262 2 998 958 40").

- Subsequent events in Q3 (page:28): "On October 19, 2026, the Company redeemed the 2027 Senior Notes with borrowings from the 2031 Revolver." The balance sheet date figures therefore pre-date that redemption, and the 2027 Senior Notes line of "600" is outstanding at September 30, 2026 but not at the report date. Same page: a dividend and a repurchase authorization declared October 27, 2026.

- Net debt in the MD&A is a company definition: page:44 "Net debt $ 4,063 $ 5,067 $ (1,004)" is total debt net of current maturities and issuance costs, and is not net of cash. It differs from the "net bank leverage" metric in the releases.

- Covenant disclosure: the Q1, Q2 and Q3 reports do not contain a covenant table or a compliance statement. A text search of those three reports for "compliant" and "interest coverage ratio" returned no hits. Only the risk-factor and forward-looking statement language about covenants appears.
#### Earnings releases, Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 (Exhibit 99.1)
- Authority: management-prepared, furnished; they provide attributed claims and non-GAAP reconciliations. They do not override the 10-Qs.

- Q3 release page:1 states "Record net revenue of $696 million, up $13 million or 2%" and "We ended the third quarter of 2026 with net bank leverage of 3.8x". The Q1 and Q2 releases state net bank leverage of 3.8x and 3.7x respectively. No source defines how net bank leverage is computed or reconciles it to the covenant ratio; the Q3 10-Q page:44 net debt figure is total debt net of current maturities and issuance costs and does not net cash.
- Q3 release page:3 repeats the credit agreement events: the eighth amendment closed on September 25, 2026 and a new 2033 term loan was entered.

- Guidance: a search for "guidance" and "outlook" found no hit in the three releases; the hits in the filings are accounting-standard text. No management guidance for the remainder of 2026 or beyond is therefore supplied. The Q3 10-Q page:43 gives expected 2026 project capital of "approximately $160 to $180 million".

The view is restricted in three respects: covenant levels are available only at December 31, 2025; the governing legal documents are not in the pack; and the last-twelve-months build mixes sources printed to one decimal (FY2025) with whole-million sources. No restriction blocks the downstream modules.

- April 21, 2026: agreement to buy the Preakness and Black-Eyed Susan intellectual property for 85 million, subject to closing conditions (Q1 10-Q page:20). The Q2 and Q3 reports and releases do not mention it, and no investing outflow of that size appears in nine months 2026, so closing status is not supplied.
### Evidence-based interpretation by dimension
#### Leverage

On the method used here, gross leverage fell from 4.28x at December 31, 2025 to 3.81x at September 30, 2026 and net leverage from 4.11x to 3.68x. Secured debt (revolver, Term Loan A and Term Loan B) is 1,648, which is 1.32x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA gross, and about 34.7% of total debt. At December 31, 2025 the company reported a covenant secured net leverage ratio of 1.4x against a limit of 4.0x. The same secured-debt arithmetic on year-end figures gives 1.54x net of unrestricted cash, so covenant definitions (EBITDA, cash netting, letters of credit) differ from the metric computed here by an unexplained margin. Evidence to risk to implication: Adjusted EBITDA includes affiliate EBITDA that is not cash to the issuer, so leverage on a cash basis is higher than the ratios above; the subsequent-event shift of 600 of notes to the revolver does not change total debt but raises the secured share.
#### Coverage

Last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA covers net interest expense 4.34x and cash interest 4.54x. For comparison, the company's reported covenant interest coverage at December 31, 2025 was 3.9x against a 2.5x minimum, and the simple FY2025 ratio of Adjusted EBITDA to interest expense is 4.05x. The covenant figure is lower than the simple ratio; possible causes are a narrower covenant EBITDA or a broader interest definition, but neither is verified because the definitions are not supplied. Headroom at September 30, 2026 is Not calculable because neither the covenant figure nor its definition is printed for any 2026 date.
#### Cash flow quality

Last-twelve-months operating cash flow of 755.8 less capital expenditures of 225.9 gives free cash flow of 529.9 before dividends and buybacks. Capital project spending fell from 172 to 119 across nine months, and FY2025 project spending of 204.7 itself followed 463.4 in FY2024 (10-K page:79); falling project capital lifts free cash flow relative to those years. Equity-method income in Adjusted EBITDA (143 in nine months 2026, Q3 10-Q page:26) exceeded distributions received (106, page:4), a 37 difference that is earnings, not cash, in the period. Cash taxes rose from 17 to 65 in nine months, reducing operating cash flow.
#### Liquidity

Unrestricted cash 167 plus computed revolver availability 1,111 gives 1,278 at September 30, 2026. After the October 19, 2026 redemption, illustrative availability is 511 and liquidity 678 if no other revolver or cash movement occurred, which cannot be confirmed from the sources. Cash at October 19, 2026 is not supplied. Near-term maturities after the redemption: next note maturity January 15, 2028.
#### Data quality

The sums tested above tie: the Q3 balance sheet, both Adjusted EBITDA reconciliations, the segment and quarterly totals and the capital expenditure table. Units differ (one decimal versus whole millions). Derived last-twelve-months figures inherit rounding of up to about 0.5 per whole-million input. The net debt line in the MD&A (4,063) is total debt net of current maturities and issuance costs, not net of cash.
#### Definition risks

(1) Adjusted EBITDA includes proportionate equity-affiliate EBITDA and noncontrolling interest EBITDA and excludes stock-based compensation, pre-opening expense and "other charges"; (2) "net bank leverage" is undefined; (3) covenant ratios use agreement definitions not supplied; (4) "Net debt" in the MD&A excludes cash netting; (5) restricted cash of 92 is excluded from liquidity because the sources do not state what it is restricted for; the 65 account wagering deposits liability (page:20) is a possible but unconfirmed link.
#### Key gaps
See Gaps. The material ones are covenant headroom at September 30, 2026, guarantor and restricted-group perimeter, redemption price of the 2027 notes and Preakness closing status.
### Downstream readiness
| Consumer | View | Basis |
| CP-1A | Sufficient with limits | Statements, Adjusted EBITDA bridge, segment data and cash-paid lines are printed; stand-alone Q2 and Q3 cash flow items must be derived from cumulative lines |
| CP-2 | Sufficient with limits | Facility-level debt, maturities, revolver availability and subsequent events are located; covenant headroom and legal terms are not |
| CP-5 | Sufficient with limits | Cash flow, shareholder returns and definition risks are located; management guidance beyond project capital is not supplied |
## Calculations
All inputs are as printed. FY2025 inputs are to one decimal and 2026 and 9M 2025 inputs to whole millions, so results carry rounding of about 0.5 per whole-million input.
1. Last-twelve-months (LTM) to September 30, 2026 = FY2025 + 9M 2026 - 9M 2025.
- Interest expense, net: 297.7 + 211 - 222 = 286.7.
- Cash paid for interest: 294.5 + 173 - 193 = 274.5.
- Operating cash flow: 769.8 + 660 - 674 = 755.8.

- Capital expenditures (maintenance plus project): FY2025 70.2 + 204.7 = 274.9; 9M 2026 57 + 119 = 176; 9M 2025 53 + 172 = 225; LTM 274.9 + 176 - 225 = 225.9. The 176 and 225 tie to the segment capital expenditure table (Q3 10-Q p27).
- Free cash flow before dividends and buybacks: 755.8 - 225.9 = 529.9.
2. Fourth-quarter 2025 implied Adjusted EBITDA = 1,205.3 - 958 = 247.3 (derived; mixed units; not printed as a discrete quarter).

3. Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation check, FY2025: 385.5 + 233.1 + 297.7 + 146.9 + 30.2 + 11.7 + 10.1 + 5.1 + 47.5 + 38.6 - 1.1 = 1,205.3, equal to the printed total. Nine months 2026: 405 + 176 + 211 + 147 + 19 + 7 + 2 + 6 + 28 - 3 = 998, equal to the printed total.
4. Leverage at September 30, 2026: total debt 4,748; unrestricted cash 167; net 4,581. Gross 4,748 / 1,245.3 = 3.81x; net 4,581 / 1,245.3 = 3.68x.
5. Leverage at December 31, 2025: total debt 5,155.1 (10-K MD&A table); unrestricted cash 200.6; net 4,954.5. Gross 5,155.1 / 1,205.3 = 4.28x; net 4,954.5 / 1,205.3 = 4.11x.

6. Secured debt at September 30, 2026 = 79 + 1,069 + 500 = 1,648 (equals the 1.6 billion floating-rate figure at Q3 10-Q p49). Share of total debt 1,648 / 4,748 = 34.7%; notes 3,100 / 4,748 = 65.3%. Gross secured leverage 1,648 / 1,245.3 = 1.32x; net of unrestricted cash (1,648 - 167) / 1,245.3 = 1.19x.

7. Secured leverage at December 31, 2025 on the same method: secured 657 + 1,112 + 286 = 2,055; net of cash 200.6 = 1,854.4; / 1,205.3 = 1.54x. Netting total cash and restricted cash of 288.5 instead gives (2,055 - 288.5) / 1,205.3 = 1.47x. The company printed 1.4x (10-K p69).

9. Revolver availability = 1,200 - 79 - 10 = 1,111 (reported 1.1 billion). Liquidity = 167 + 1,111 = 1,278. Illustrative post-redemption: revolver drawn 79 + 600 = 679; availability 1,200 - 679 - 10 = 511; liquidity 511 + 167 = 678. This assumes no other movement and a redemption at principal with no accrued interest funded by the revolver, neither of which the sources state.

10. Coupon run-rate on notes at September 30, 2026: 600 x 5.50% = 33.00; 700 x 4.75% = 33.25; 1,200 x 5.75% = 69.00; 600 x 6.75% = 40.50; total 175.75. After the 2027 redemption: 33.25 + 69.00 + 40.50 = 142.75. The credit agreement 12-month estimate of 149 (page:47) compares with 1,648 x 5.48% = 90.3 of interest plus quarterly amortization of roughly 60 (1.25% x 1,100 x 4 = 55; 0.25% x 500 x 4 = 5), about 150; this reading of the 149 is an analyst inference and not stated in the filing.

11. Springing-maturity test dates (maturity less 91 days): 2028 notes January 15, 2028 gives October 16, 2027; 2030 notes April 1, 2030 gives December 31, 2029; 2031 notes May 1, 2031 gives January 30, 2031. The 2027 notes (April 1, 2027) would have given December 31, 2026 but were redeemed on October 19, 2026.

12. Equity affiliates: Gaming segment equity income within Adjusted EBITDA 143 for nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q p26) against distributions received 106 (p4): difference 37. Share of total Adjusted EBITDA 143 / 998 = 14.3%.
13. Cash taxes LTM, net of refunds: 63.6 + 65 - (17 - 1) = 112.6.
14. Shareholder distributions nine months 2026: dividends 31 + repurchases 44 = 75.
15. Current maturities at September 30, 2026: 659 less the 600 2027 notes = 59, close to scheduled amortization of 55 on Term Loan A plus 5 on Term Loan B; this attribution is an analyst inference.

| Stand-alone Q2 and Q3 2026 cash flow lines are not printed; derivable from cumulative columns | Low | CP-1A | Derive downstream with rounding caveat |
| Preakness IP purchase of 85 million: closing status and funding Not supplied | Low | CP-2 | Check the next filing |
| Defined-benefit pension and retiree medical obligations: none located by text search, so Not supplied | Low | CP-2 | Confirm absence in 10-K note 17 and the exhibits |
| Recourse to the issuer for affiliate debt of 760: Not supplied | Low | CP-2 | Read affiliate guarantee disclosure if any |
| Unit mix: FY2025 to one decimal versus whole millions in 2026 | Low | CP-1A | Carry rounding caveat |

CP-1A, then CP-2 and CP-5 per the dependency order. Carry forward: the LTM base figures and their calculation steps above; the subsequent-event treatment of the 2027 notes redemption (balance sheet figures at September 30, 2026 still show the notes outstanding); the springing-maturity test dates; the equity-affiliate share of Adjusted EBITDA; and the covenant gap. ### Business and transaction view

Churchill Downs Incorporated is a Kentucky-incorporated, Nasdaq-listed operator whose earnings come from three segments: Live and Historical Racing, Wagering Services and Solutions, and Gaming. Live and Historical Racing, which combines the Kentucky Derby franchise with historical racing machine venues in Kentucky, Virginia and New Hampshire, is the largest segment by revenue and Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026. Gaming is the second largest and carries the equity income from two unconsolidated casinos. The company is publicly owned with no controlling holder disclosed in the supplied text, so no sponsor behaviour is inferred; governance is assessed from documented issuer actions only. The most important transaction fact for a creditor is the July 29, 2026 announcement that the company is exploring a sale of nine wholly owned regional gaming properties, set against a recently refinanced bank structure, a pending note redemption funded by the revolver, an active growth capital program and a larger buyback authorization. These pull in different directions for creditors: asset-sale proceeds and lower buybacks would reduce leverage, while the growth program and buybacks would absorb cash. Confidence is Medium because the sale has no disclosed terms.

### Credit translations

1. Concentration and seasonality. Evidence: nine-month 2026 historical racing revenue of 780 is 33.3% of group revenue, Churchill Downs Racetrack revenue is 262 in nine months but 12 in Q3, and the second quarter produced 477 of the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 998 (47.8%). Mechanic: earnings and the revolver draw are tied to the Derby calendar and to Virginia and Kentucky machine regulation, so a stand-alone quarter misstates run-rate and one regulatory or tax change can move group cash flow. Implication: leverage tolerance and liquidity should be judged on LTM and seasonal-peak working capital, and monitoring should track Virginia tax and competition. No logged conflict counters this.

2. Portfolio review. Evidence: the Q3 10-Q p32 statement and the Gaming segment Adjusted EBITDA of 384 for nine months, of which 143 is equity income that would not be part of a sale of wholly owned properties. Mechanic: a sale of 280 to 300 of annual Adjusted EBITDA removes 22.5% to 24.1% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 1,245.3. At the 3.68x net leverage of CP-1, proceeds of about 1,030 to 1,104 would be needed to leave net leverage unchanged if all proceeds repaid debt and nothing else changed; this is an illustrative threshold, not a valuation or a forecast. Implication: the debt-reduction benefit depends on proceeds, tax leakage and any mandatory prepayment or collateral-release terms, none supplied; the remaining company would be more concentrated in racing and historical racing machines. No logged conflict counters this.

3. Capital allocation. Evidence: FY2025 outflows exceeded free cash flow with net borrowings of 216.4, followed by 2026 deleveraging and a 750 authorization. Mechanic: buybacks are discretionary and can be paced to leverage; project capital is guided at 160 to 180 for 2026 with Rockingham at 180 to 200 and a 280 to 300 Churchill Downs Racetrack building announced (10-K p58). Implication: no sponsor-style extraction is evident, but the board has shown it will let total debt rise while returning cash and buying assets, so monitoring posture should follow leverage targets and revolver usage. No logged conflict counters this.
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The refinancing completed in the quarter has four parts. On September 25, 2026 the company closed the eighth amendment to its credit agreement, extending the maturity of the revolver and Term Loan A from July 2029 to September 2031, removing the 10 basis point credit spread adjustment and amending other provisions, with the extension subject to a springing maturity if notes or other material debt maturing before September 25, 2031 are not refinanced at least 91 days before maturity (Q3 10-Q page:14). On the same date it entered a new 500 million senior secured term loan B due September 25, 2033 under the credit agreement, issued at 99.875% of principal at SOFR plus 175 basis points with quarterly amortization of 0.25% of the original balance; net proceeds were used to repay the Term Loan B-1 due 2028, to repay revolver borrowings, to pay fees and for working capital and general corporate purposes (page:14 and page:15). Debt issuance costs of 7 were paid in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:4). Third, on September 18, 2026 the company issued a conditional notice to redeem the 600 million 5.50% senior notes due April 1, 2027, and on October 19, 2026 it redeemed them with revolver borrowings, a subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet (pages 16 and 28). The redemption price and accrued interest are not supplied. Fourth, it declared an annual dividend of $0.469 per share payable January 5, 2027 and approved a new 750 million repurchase program that includes the 306 million remaining under the prior program (page:28).

No new bond issuance is disclosed in the supplied sources. The net effect on structure is that secured bank debt increases while unsecured note debt falls: after the 2027 notes redemption the next note maturity is the 700 million 4.75% notes due January 15, 2028, and the springing-maturity test for those notes falls on or about October 16, 2027 on the 91-day wording (CP-1 calculation). Executed amendment text, guarantor identities and the redemption price are the main missing documents.

Other transactions with creditor relevance: the exploration of a sale of nine wholly owned gaming properties announced on July 29, 2026 (page:32), the pending 85 million purchase of the Preakness and Black-Eyed Susan intellectual property announced April 21, 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:20, closing status not supplied in later sources), the August 2026 purchase of the 49% United Tote interest (cash flow line of 31 for acquisition of noncontrolling interest, Q3 10-Q page:4) and the Rockingham Grand Casino redevelopment with a mid-2027 opening (10-K page:11). Other developments in the sources include the Louisiana historical racing ruling and the Virginia tax change described above.

| CP-5 | Ready with limitations | Concentration, seasonality, governance behaviour and the logged absence of conflicts | Evidence review and committee challenge need the points of weakest evidence | Ownership, guarantor identity and covenant headroom are Insufficient Information | Flag the portfolio review and covenant headroom as the key challenge points |
## Calculations
2. Historical racing revenue 780 / 2,339 = 33.3%. Virginia revenue 410 / 2,339 = 17.5%. Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA 477 / nine-month 998 = 47.8%.
3. Portfolio review weight: 280 / 1,245.3 = 22.5% and 300 / 1,245.3 = 24.1% (LTM Adjusted EBITDA from CP-1).

4. Leverage-neutral proceeds: net debt 4,581 / LTM Adjusted EBITDA 1,245.3 = 3.679x (CP-1); 3.679 x 280 = 1,030 and 3.679 x 300 = 1,104. Illustrative only; assumes all proceeds repay debt, no tax or transaction costs and no change in other items.

5. FY2025 sources and uses: free cash flow 769.8 - 274.9 = 494.9; less dividends 30.8, repurchases 427.8, share-settlement taxes 17.0 and acquisition of gaming rights 185.3 leaves -166.0. Net borrowings = proceeds 1,098.1 - repayments 881.7 = 216.4, equal to the change in total debt 5,155.1 - 4,938.7 = 216.4. Reconciliation to the cash change of 35.8: -166.0 + 216.4 - 0.3 debt issuance costs - 2.3 overdraft - 0.7 other financing - 11.3 other investing = 35.8. Dividends plus repurchases = 30.8 + 427.8 = 458.6.
6. Nine months 2026 debt change: 4,748 - 5,155 = -407 (Q3 10-Q p13).

7. Wholly owned versus equity Gaming Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026: 384 - 143 = 241, ignoring 1 of other income; not comparable to the annual 280 to 300 because that figure includes sportsbook and market access in another segment and is annual.

9. Announced growth amounts: Rockingham 180 to 200 (10-K p11), Churchill Downs Racetrack new building 280 to 300 (10-K p58) and Preakness purchase 85 (Q1 10-Q p20): low 180 + 280 + 85 = 545; high 200 + 300 + 85 = 585. Timing differs by project and not all is committed capital.
8. TLB proceeds at issue price: 500 x 99.875% = 499.375 before fees; capitalized costs 5 for the loan and 2 for the amendment, total 7, matching the cash flow line (Q3 10-Q p4, p14).

spans.text: ## Request

Churchill Downs Incorporated (context name Churchill Downs Inc, ticker CHDN), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. This module synthesises the fundamental credit view from the settled financial base and the business and transaction context, in USD, on the consolidated perimeter, with an evidence cutoff of 2026-11-05.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on
This module works from upstream handoffs only and quotes no source text. The seven pinned sources below underlie those handoffs and were not re-read here.

| EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl | bbdcb62a4845e34e0fdd4338c48e18f02c4eceb2b21c6ecefed1bd7b13c21521 |
| EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl | 85b22b14ac2149df8072938d3dbc3e8d85579a1e2355ea8fce27bcd305c203d4 |

The context file (sha256 7c4f52e55b5e23c0fba0c45fbf91c794297fbfceecf1db4e9e336166f978aca8) holds run settings only and is not issuer evidence.

| CP-1 | 1ca790f594af2528c57d0f57a2e49328f2a2f28e48929edda12648fa238cae8e | Financial base: last-twelve-months (LTM) figures, debt register, liquidity, calculations |

Consistency with upstream: CP-1A supplements CP-1 with the July 29, 2026 portfolio review, which CP-1 omitted; this module uses both. This module also refines one CP-1A point: the USD 37 million gap between equity-affiliate contribution to Adjusted EBITDA (USD 143 million) and distributions received (USD 106 million) splits into USD 28 million of affiliate interest, depreciation and amortization added back in Adjusted EBITDA and USD 9 million of equity income not yet distributed (see Calculations). No upstream figure is otherwise contradicted.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Churchill Downs has a sound but still-moving credit profile: leverage fell, cash flow is strong and liquidity is ample, while a planned asset sale, large buybacks and 2028 note refinancing will decide the direction. | Medium | The asset sale has no disclosed terms, and covenant headroom and executed debt documents are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net leverage on last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.11x to 3.68x as debt fell by USD 407 million in nine months. | Supports the credit; the improvement rests on repayments funded by operating cash flow and reduced buybacks. | High |
| Last-twelve-months free cash flow was USD 529.9 million, and Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest 4.54x. | Debt service capacity is strong at current earnings. | Medium |

| The company is exploring a sale of nine gaming properties with USD 280 to 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA. | Proceeds of about USD 1,030 to 1,104 million would be needed to keep leverage unchanged. | Medium |

| The 2027 notes were redeemed with the revolver, and bank maturities spring earlier if the 2028 notes are not refinanced by about October 2027. | Refinancing the USD 700 million 2028 notes is the nearest structural test. | Medium |

| Earnings rely on Virginia, historical racing machines and the Derby quarter, and Adjusted EBITDA includes affiliate income that is not all cash. | Concentration and earnings quality limit how much weight leverage ratios can bear. | Medium |
### Credit view

Churchill Downs Incorporated is a sound, moderately leveraged credit whose direction depends on how it uses the next year's cash. The strongest support is deleveraging: net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.11x to 3.68x, free cash flow was USD 529.9 million and liquidity was USD 1,278 million at September 30, 2026. The weakest point is that the cushion can be spent: a USD 750 million buyback authorization, USD 545 to 585 million of announced projects and a possible sale of assets worth USD 280 to 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA all compete with debt reduction, while the 2027 notes now sit on the revolver. The outcome turns on sale proceeds, buyback pace and refinancing the 2028 notes before about October 2027. Confidence: Medium.
### Key findings

Churchill Downs reduced total debt from USD 5,155 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 4,748 million at September 30, 2026, and its net leverage on LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,245.3 million fell from 4.11x to 3.68x (gross 4.28x to 3.81x). The reduction came from operating cash flow of USD 660 million in nine months after capital expenditures of USD 176 million, and from sharply lower buybacks of USD 44 million against USD 396 million a year earlier. LTM free cash flow before distributions was USD 529.9 million, and Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest 4.54x, up from 4.09x at year-end 2025.

The most consequential new fact is the July 29, 2026 announcement that the company is exploring a sale of nine wholly owned gaming properties representing USD 280 to 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA, or 22.5% to 24.1% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA. At the current 3.68x net leverage, sale proceeds of roughly USD 1,030 to 1,104 million used to repay debt would leave leverage unchanged; any lower price would raise it, any higher price would reduce it. Terms, buyer, timetable and use of proceeds are not disclosed, and the creditor consequences of mandatory prepayment or collateral release cannot be assessed without the credit agreement.

The September 2026 refinancing extended the revolver and Term Loan A to September 2031 and added a USD 500 million term loan B due 2033 that retired the 2028 term loan, but it left a springing maturity: if notes maturing before September 25, 2031 are not refinanced 91 days ahead, the bank debt matures earlier. For the USD 700 million 2028 notes that date is about October 16, 2027. The USD 600 million 2027 notes were redeemed on October 19, 2026 with revolver borrowings, a subsequent event; illustratively that cuts revolver availability from USD 1,111 million to USD 511 million and liquidity from USD 1,278 million to USD 678 million if nothing else changed. Even so, computed secured net leverage after the redemption is about 1.67x against a December 2025 covenant limit of 4.0x, and the reported December 2025 interest coverage of 3.9x compares with a 2.5x minimum, so maintenance covenant pressure is not evident, although 2026 covenant figures are not supplied.

Earnings quality and concentration deserve weight. Live and Historical Racing is 49.1% of nine-month 2026 revenue, historical racing machines 33.3% and Virginia 17.5%, and Virginia faces competition and a new state tax from July 1, 2026. The second quarter produced 47.8% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA because of the Derby. Adjusted EBITDA adds the issuer's share of affiliate EBITDA, so USD 28 million of affiliate interest, depreciation and amortization and USD 9 million of undistributed equity income in nine months 2026 are not cash to the issuer.

Capital allocation is the governance question. In FY2025 shareholder returns, share-settlement taxes and the gaming rights acquisition exceeded free cash flow by USD 166.0 million and total debt rose by USD 216.4 million. In 2026 debt fell, but the board approved a USD 750 million repurchase program on October 27, 2026 and raised the dividend. No sponsor or related-party extraction is evident, and no leverage target or creditor-protection policy is stated in the supplied sources.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Churchill Downs operates Churchill Downs Racetrack, home of the Kentucky Derby, within a diversified portfolio across racing, historical racing, online wagering and regional casinos, with three segments each producing Adjusted EBITDA. Cash conversion is strong: LTM operating cash flow of USD 755.8 million is 60.7% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow is 42.6%. Gross leverage on the LTM basis has fallen at every quarter-end of 2026, from 4.28x in December 2025 to 4.07x in March, 3.86x in June and 3.81x in September 2026. Liquidity of USD 1,278 million and maintenance covenants with wide computed cushions give room, and the bank maturity extension to 2031, subject to the springing maturity, removes near-term bank refinancing. At September 30, 2026 about 34.7% of debt was secured and 65.3% was unsecured notes, and after the October 2026 redemption no note matures until January 2028.

Weaknesses. Leverage of 3.68x net is still material for a seasonal, regulation-exposed business, and the company's own net bank leverage metric of 3.8x is undefined. Earnings are concentrated in the Derby quarter, historical racing machines and Virginia. Adjusted EBITDA includes affiliate EBITDA and excludes stock compensation, pre-opening and other charges, and covenant EBITDA is not supplied. The springing maturity ties USD 2,248 million of illustrative post-redemption secured debt, being the term loan A, term loan B and revolver, to note refinancing. Buybacks and projects are discretionary but large, and the portfolio review would remove about a quarter of earnings before any deleveraging is certain.
### Credit assessment
| Item | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Fundamental credit view: sound, moderately leveraged and deleveraging, with direction set by the asset sale, buyback pace and 2028 note refinancing | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, coverage and liquidity figures; CP-1A portfolio review, governance and timeline rows |

| Thesis | Strong cash conversion and a deleveraging record support the credit, but concentration, earnings quality and discretionary capital allocation mean leverage can move either way | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 calculations; CP-1A concentration and capital allocation rows |
| Business risk | Moderate: diversified by segment but concentrated by quarter, machine product and state | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A operating model and credit translations |

| Financial risk and liquidity | Moderate and improving, with revolver reliance rising after October 19, 2026 | Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the rating of risk | Medium | CP-1 figures |
| Governance | Mixed: documented debt-funded outlays in FY2025, deleveraging in 2026, new buyback authorization | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A governance rows |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Portfolio review outcome | Sale of nine properties removes USD 280 to 300 million of annual Adjusted EBITDA; leverage-neutral proceeds are USD 1,030 to 1,104 million | Leverage could rise if proceeds are below that range or are not used for debt; collateral release and prepayment terms unknown | Material |

| 2028 note refinancing and springing maturity | Bank debt matures early if the 2028 notes are not refinanced 91 days ahead (about October 16, 2027) | Refinancing risk concentrated in the next 12 months for USD 700 million of notes and USD 2,248 million of secured debt on an illustrative basis | Material |

| Revolver reliance | The 2027 notes were refinanced on the revolver, reducing illustrative availability to USD 511 million | Less liquidity buffer for the Derby working-capital cycle and for projects | Material |

| Shareholder returns | A USD 750 million authorization includes USD 306 million already available; FY2025 returns were partly debt-funded | Buybacks can offset deleveraging and raise leverage tolerance without creditor consent | Material |

| Earnings concentration | Virginia 17.5% of revenue, historical racing machines 33.3%, second quarter 47.8% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA | A regulatory, tax or competitive shock hits cash flow and covenants quickly | Material |

| Earnings quality | Adjusted EBITDA includes USD 28 million of affiliate interest, depreciation and amortization and excludes recurring items such as stock compensation (USD 19 million in nine months 2026) | Leverage on cash EBITDA is higher than reported ratios | Minor |
| Covenant visibility | Latest covenant figures are December 31, 2025; later headroom is Not supplied | Cannot confirm compliance trend; computed cushions are wide | Minor |

| Growth capital | Rockingham, a new Churchill Downs Racetrack building and the Preakness purchase total USD 545 to 585 million | Competes with debt reduction; completion risk and timing differ by project | Minor |
## Calculations
All inputs come from the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, which cite the filings. FY2025 inputs are to one decimal and 2026 inputs are whole millions, so results carry rounding.

1. Secured debt after the October 19, 2026 redemption, illustrative: 1,648 + 600 = 2,248 (USD millions); secured net leverage (2,248 - 167) / 1,245.3 = 1.67x. This assumes the redemption was funded at principal entirely by the revolver and no other balance changed.

2. Interest-coverage cushion: reported December 31, 2025 coverage 3.9x against a 2.5x minimum; EBITDA could fall by (3.9 - 2.5) / 3.9 = 35.9% with interest unchanged before the covenant ratio reached the minimum. On the simple LTM ratio of 4.34x (1,245.3 / 286.7) the equivalent fall is 1 - 2.5 / 4.34 = 42.4%, to EBITDA of 716.8. Covenant definitions are not supplied, so these are indicative only.
3. Cash conversion: LTM operating cash flow 755.8 / 1,245.3 = 60.7%; LTM free cash flow 529.9 / 1,245.3 = 42.6%.
4. Leverage trend, from CP-1 chart data: gross 4.28x (December 2025), 4.07x (March 2026), 3.86x (June 2026), 3.81x (September 2026); net 4.11x, 3.90x, 3.70x, 3.68x.

5. Equity-affiliate bridge, nine months 2026: Adjusted EBITDA contribution 143 = equity income in the income statement 115 + affiliate interest, depreciation and amortization 28; distributions received 106; undistributed equity income 115 - 106 = 9; 143 - 106 = 37 = 28 + 9. Distributions as a share of equity income 106 / 115 = 92.2%.
6. FY2025 funding gap: free cash flow 494.9 less dividends 30.8, repurchases 427.8, share-settlement taxes 17.0 and acquisition of gaming rights 185.3 = -166.0; net borrowings 216.4.
7. Portfolio review weight and leverage-neutral proceeds: 280 / 1,245.3 = 22.5%; 300 / 1,245.3 = 24.1%; 3.679 x 280 = 1,030; 3.679 x 300 = 1,104 (illustrative, all proceeds repaying debt).
8. Debt change: 4,748 - 5,155 = -407. Growth amounts: 545 to 585.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |
